explained.headline: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over suspected Chinese spy ties

happened.text: Nvidia opened an independent investigation after reports that its chief executive Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
The company's board of directors stated that it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised by the affair.
Republican lawmakers asked Jensen Huang to appear before congressional committees to discuss security protocols against foreign espionage.

matters.text: The sources state that Nvidia's microchips are a cornerstone of the artificial intelligence boom and central to the technological rivalry between the United States and China.
The board of directors declared that prioritising United States national and economic security is paramount to the interests of the company and its shareholders.

uncertain.text: It remains unclear what specific information Alice Huang allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable that material was, or when her intelligence gathering began.
China has rejected the espionage allegations entirely, describing the claims as groundless speculation intended to smear the country.

terms.definition: A solid material whose electrical conductivity can be controlled, used widely in computer microchips.

removed.text: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the microchip manufacturer for more than thirty years.
Nvidia is valued at approximately $4.5 trillion and is central to manufacturing hardware for emerging artificial intelligence technologies.
Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and apologised, while stating that he would fully cooperate with the board's inquiry.
why: Jensen Huang apologised for infidelity, but the evidence does not state he promised to cooperate with the board.

removed.text: US intelligence officials believed that Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based data centre firm named Megaspeed, was a spy for Beijing.
why: The evidence does not confirm Alice Huang was an executive at a company called Megaspeed.

explained.headline: G7 ministers meet in Paris to discuss Ukraine and Iran

happened.text: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven leading industrialised nations met in Paris for two days of talks.
Negotiations between Ukraine and Russia under United States mediation were scheduled to begin in Abu Dhabi.
Iranian officials submitted a new nuclear and peace proposal through Qatari mediators.

background.text: The Group of Seven brings together Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Relations between Washington and Tehran have been severely strained since the United States withdrew from the Iran nuclear deal in 2018 under President Donald Trump.

matters.text: European governments have insisted that any settlement to end the conflict in Ukraine must include European participation and preserve Ukrainian sovereignty.
US President Donald Trump stated that the war in Ukraine could soon end and suggested that the country might emerge from a settlement with altered borders.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul urged Washington and Moscow to pursue concrete negotiations rather than military escalation.

uncertain.text: It remains unclear how exactly European representatives will take part in the upcoming negotiations in Abu Dhabi.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that negotiations with Iran had not made significant progress and described Iranian demands as unrealistic.
The United States has not ruled out resuming military strikes against Iran if diplomatic efforts fail.

An international organisation that seeks to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy and inhibit its use for military purposes.

why: The evidence does not confirm Marco Rubio attended the meetings.

explained.headline: Pope Leo XIV urges social protection during Argentina visit

happened.text: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Buenos Aires on a Latin American tour and urged President Javier Milei to ensure the economy benefits the poor.
The pontiff stated that the economy must serve the people and stressed the needs of households struggling despite hard work.
During his address, the Pope made a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.
In response, Javier Milei defended his libertarian policies by stating that individual rights form the backbone of the constitution.

background.text: Javier Milei is the president of Argentina who came to office promising to revive the economy and tame runaway inflation by shrinking the welfare state.
Pope Leo XIV is the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics and is undertaking a 12-day tour of Latin America following lung cancer surgery.
Javier Milei previously used harsh language against Pope Francis, though he struck a conciliatory tone toward his predecessor upon Leo's arrival.

matters.text: Observers note that the visit serves as a litmus test of support for the church in a country where the proportion of Catholics has declined significantly.
Citizens have expressed hope that the pontiff's presence might help unite a country bitterly divided over austerity and politics.
The papal visit carries political significance ahead of Argentina's presidential election, in which Javier Milei has stated he will seek another term.

uncertain.text: It remains to be seen whether the papal appeals will alter the administration's contentious fiscal policies or bridge the deep political divisions in the country.

terms.definition: Another title for the Pope, the Bishop of Rome and leader of the worldwide Catholic Church.

explained.headline: Trump calls Dana White press secretary offer a joke

happened.text: US President Donald Trump told reporters on Sunday that he was only kidding after previously announcing on his Truth Social platform that he had offered the role of White House press secretary to the Ultimate Fighting Championship boss Dana White.
Trump stated that while the invitation was just a little fun and that he had only been joking, White loved the idea.

background.text: Dana White is the chief executive officer of the Ultimate Fighting Championship and a long-standing friend of Donald Trump who has spoken at multiple Republican National Conventions.
The press secretary position became vacant in October after Katie Zacharia quit the job after less than five days.

matters.text: The playful job offer followed heavy Republican losses in the midterm elections, in which the party lost its majority in both houses of Congress.

uncertain.text: Trump did not specify exactly who told him that making the Ultimate Fighting Championship boss his spokesperson was a good idea.
German broadcaster Tagesschau reported that the cable news network CNN stated White had turned down the post, whereas Trump maintained that White was visiting Washington for other reasons.

terms.definition: A major American mixed martial arts promotion company that hosts professional cage-fighting events.
A senior official who acts as the primary spokesperson for the United States government administration and the president.

removed.text: In his original social media post, the president had asked White to take the job and bring several mixed martial arts fighters as assistants to defend against the left.
Trump claimed that after he made the mock announcement, people told him it was actually a pretty good idea.
Katie Zacharia had taken over the post from Karoline Leavitt, who served as press secretary from the start of the second presidential term until her resignation in August.
why: Evidence states Leavitt left in October, not August. The claim timeline is incorrect.

removed.text: It remained unclear whether Dana White would accept any other position, as he declined to state during a news conference whether he would take the vacant post during their planned Monday meeting.
why: White did not decline the post explicitly; he said he has many jobs.
